basis: Motor-neuron degeneration and sensorineural hearing loss define MMND; muscle wasting reflects denervation; optic atrophy occurs in <30%.
Inherited elevated alpha-tryptase with mast-cell-mediated symptoms; common direct damage to other organs is not established.
Congenital failure of neutrophil production causes severe neutropenia and immunodeficiency; bacterial infections are separate sequelae.
B-cell maturation failure with near-absent B cells; neutropenia reported in 30-79%. Infections and secondary bronchiectasis are separately diagnosed sequelae.
Developmental delay and intellectual disability in 17/17; joint hypermobility in 8/17 does not establish joint damage; hearing impairment in 3/17.
Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy affects cardiac muscle.
Congenital protein-losing enteropathy; renal dysplasia and ocular coloboma each reported in 1/1. Electrolyte abnormalities reflect enteric losses; evidence is limited.
Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection involving skin; pulmonary disease is not intrinsic to the cutaneous concept.
Variable reproductive/sex-development phenotype; mixed blood lineages and pigmentation do not establish damage. Consistent urinary or endocrine dysfunction is not established.
Inflammatory liver disease; infectious and autoimmune mechanisms apply only to particular subtypes.
Benign tumour arising in cutaneous sweat glands.
Isolated congenital abnormality of bronchial sidedness; associated heterotaxy defects are outside this isolated concept.
Hereditary recurrent peripheral facial nerve palsy.
Bone disorder by explicit ancestry; no evidence supports additional organs or a metabolic mechanism.
Familial early-onset Alzheimer disease causes cerebral neurodegeneration and dementia.
Congenital defect of the atrioventricular septum.
CSTA-related epidermal fragility, peeling and hyperkeratosis; nail changes remain within the skin axis.
Defining obesity, intellectual disability and ocular defects; femoral bowing/abnormal ossification in 30-79%. Frequent dental defects omitted because of the four-axis cap.
Congenital univentricular cardiac anatomy with a single atrioventricular valve.
Defining demyelinating neuropathy, progressive deafness and skeletal deformities; glaucoma reported in 2/3 patients supports ocular damage, with limited sample size.
Malformation of superficial lymphatic vessels producing cutaneous microcystic lesions; vascular ancestry supports cardiovascular classification.
RHOBTB2-related developmental and epileptic encephalopathy; seizures and developmental impairment in 10/10. Hypotonia does not establish intrinsic muscle disease.
CASK-related intellectual disability with variable brain hypoplasia and seizures; nystagmus alone does not establish direct ocular damage across the spectrum.
Debranching defect damages liver and skeletal muscle; cardiac hypertrophy/cardiomyopathy occurs in roughly 40-60%. Frequent intellectual disability/immunodeficiency are atypical.
Benign tumour arising in the pleura, which belongs to the pulmonary axis.
